notes: Tangent journeys. A tangent is a child session in this engine -- /tangent <name> switches onto one and bare /tangent returns to the parent -- so it belongs with the session journeys rather than with conversation history, and it shares the switch path that loading a session uses. What a user depends on is that the detour leaves no trace on the session they came back to, which is asserted from the transcript after the return.

scenarios.name: A tangent takes the session aside and returns it without the detour
scenarios.description: A turn on the root session, a named tangent with a turn of its own, then a return -- asserts the tangent is entered and marked, and that returning restores the root transcript without the tangent's turns
steps: prompt:this is the tangent turn TANGENTWORD-2
scenarios.observe: The tangent is entered by name and the run only proceeds once the session says so, so the detour is real rather than assumed. The return is the assertion that matters: the root answer is still there while the tangent's answer is not, which is what separates a session that came back from one that merely carried on. The negative names the status chip rather than the bare tangent name, because the name also reaches the screen from the command the user typed and from the alert that confirmed the switch -- only the chip means 'still on the detour'.

scenarios.name: The tangent list states the absence, then shows the tree once one exists
scenarios.description: A tangent listing before any tangent exists and again after creating one -- asserts the empty case is stated rather than blank, and the populated case shows the tangent under its root with the current one marked
scenarios.observe: The empty listing is taken first and acts as the control: the same command, before any tangent exists, states the absence rather than opening an empty picker. After creating one the listing is a tree -- the tangent under its root -- with the active one marked, which is what tells a user where they are once several exist. The switch affordance is asserted because a list of tangents you cannot move between is only half the surface.

scenarios.name: The bare tangent command starts a named detour when there is none to leave
scenarios.description: The tangent command with no argument, issued on the root session -- asserts it opens an auto-named tangent and marks it, which is the opposite of what the same command does while already on one
scenarios.observe: The same bare command does opposite things depending on where it is issued: on a tangent it returns to the parent, and on root it opens a new one under an auto-assigned name. The session id changing is what proves a detour was actually opened rather than the command becoming a no-op at root -- the name and the placeholder hint both come from the alert the wait already saw, so on their own they would restate it. The transcript carries the parent's turn into the fork, which is the fork inheriting its history rather than evidence about the parent.

scenarios.name: Returning from a nested tangent lands on its parent and stays marked
scenarios.description: A tangent opened from inside another tangent, then a return -- asserts the return lands on the intermediate parent rather than the root, and that the session is still marked as being on a tangent
scenarios.observe: Returning from a nested tangent has two ways to go wrong and this separates them. Landing on the root instead of the intermediate parent is caught by the wait for 'Returned to alpha'. The subtler one is the marker: the session is still on a tangent after this return, so the chip must still be set, and clearing it would leave a user believing they are back on the root while their turns go to a branch. The chip is asserted for the parent and asserted absent for the branch just left, which is the pair that distinguishes 'moved up one level' from 'cleared'. The parent's own answer is asserted present because the return replays that session, not the branch's.
